client_alerts.headline: Claude Meetings beta puts an AI participant in Google Meet calls
client_alerts.body: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings in beta for Team and Enterprise plans on Nov 12. Any client on those plans can now have Claude join, hear and summarise Meet calls. Ask clients to confirm recording-consent notices, retention settings and whether BCP/DR tabletop or incident bridges are in scope **before** users switch it on.

client_alerts.headline: Anthropic regional usage policy tightened; OpenAI API now processes in India
client_alerts.body: From Nov 12 Anthropic bars Claude use by entities controlled from restricted regions including mainland China, which matters for clients with offshore subsidiaries or vendors. OpenAI reportedly began in-country API processing for India. Both change the data-residency and third-party dependency answers in client AI risk registers. Details are from aggregators and are not yet confirmed on the vendors' own pages.

top_moves.title: Anthropic ships Claude Meetings (beta) for Google Meet
top_moves.body: Claude can now join Google Meet calls on Team and Enterprise plans, with other platforms promised later. It is a direct competitor to Copilot in Teams and Gemini in Meet for meeting notes and action items.

top_moves.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory
top_moves.body: OpenAI announced cybersecurity products in which AI agents attack client systems to test them. This builds on last week's GPT-6 Cyber red-team rollout and moves AI-driven offensive testing toward a product clients can buy.

top_moves.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen and two new TPUs
top_moves.body: A first Gemini 4-family model and the TPU 8tx / 8i Max chips were reported on Nov 12. Coverage is from digests so far; wait for Google's model card before changing defaults.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory turn AI attack agents into products; India API processing goes in-country.
providers.detail: OpenAI announced Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, where agents act as attackers to probe systems. Reports say API requests from India are now processed domestically. The Nov 12 Cursor cutoff date has passed, but no confirmation that it took effect was found. ChatGPT Images 2.6 shipped Nov 4.
providers.alertReason: India in-country API processing changes data-residency answers.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Claude Meetings beta joins Google Meet calls; regional usage policy now bars China-controlled entities.
providers.detail: Claude Meetings launched in beta for Team and Enterprise on Nov 12. An updated usage policy restricting entities controlled from mainland China took effect the same day. The IPO ($70–78 range, ticker ANT) is expected to price the week of Nov 16, with trading around Nov 19. Sonnet 4.5 API retirement and Opus 4.8 fast-mode removal both land Nov 30.
providers.alertReason: Meeting-recording AI and tightened regional policy affect client governance.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen reported as the first Gemini 4-family model, alongside TPU 8tx and 8i Max.
providers.detail: A Nov 12 digest reports Gemini 4 Hydrogen and two new TPU variants. No Google blog post was found to confirm capabilities or pricing. Treat as provisional and keep current Gemini 3.5 workflows unchanged until a model card appears.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet. Still no Grok 5; Grok 4.7 remains the flagship.
providers.detail: No new model found. Developer notes list Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 and a Nov 2 retirement of grok-imagine-image-quality. SpaceXAI (as Cursor's owner) is the counterparty in the OpenAI–Cursor cutoff.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Quiet. Named in a nonprofit lawsuit seeking to halt advanced AI development.
providers.detail: No product ship found. A coalition of nonprofits sued OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX's AI division seeking to stop frontier development. Muse Spark 1.2 open weights remain promised but undated.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Quiet. Large 4 open-weight status still unconfirmed; private-cloud and on-prem Studio due late November.
providers.detail: No new release confirmed. Reports on Mistral Large 4 open weights conflict. The on-prem and private-cloud Mistral Studio rollout announced last week is still expected late November.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet today. Teammates agents (Max) and Comet patent search from last week continue rolling out.
providers.detail: No new ship found since the Nov 5 Teammates launch and Nov 6 Comet Assistant and patent search updates.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Office in Copilot (Word, Excel, PowerPoint inside the Copilot app) begins worldwide rollout mid-November; Ignite starts Nov 17.
providers.detail: Message-center item MC1530611, updated Nov 5, puts Office in Copilot GA rollout from mid-November. @Copilot in Teams enters private preview by month-end, and Autopilot rolls to Frontier. Expect more at Ignite, Nov 17–20.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Quiet. No November ship found; Haiku 5.5, local sandboxing and Ollama support from October stand.
providers.detail: No new release found this week. Usage-based billing on every plan has applied since June 1.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: OpenAI's proposed Nov 12 cutoff date has passed; no confirmation yet whether OpenAI models are gone.
providers.detail: OpenAI planned to end Cursor's model access on Nov 12 after the SpaceX acquisition (about 5% of Cursor traffic). Anthropic, Google and Grok models remain. Check the Cursor model picker before any client demo that relied on GPT models.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: Quiet. Gamma 5 (Oct 6, follow-up Oct 26) remains the latest release.
providers.detail: No November update found. Gamma 5 added an agent that builds whole decks and pulls context from Slack, Notion and Granola.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: Quiet. Notion 3.8 (Oct 13, 'Context for your agents') is still the latest.

persistent_signals.text: OpenAI — AI offensive-security agents — 2 weeks running (GPT-6 Cyber to vetted red teams last week; Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory products this week)

month_themes.then: Model-safety warnings (self-replication on IoT), insider and physical-security incidents, Anthropic IPO preparation
month_themes.now: AI in meetings and productivity suites (Claude Meetings, Office in Copilot), AI red-teaming as a product, data residency and regional policy tightening

habits.shift: No change. If Claude Meetings is enabled, use it to capture tabletop debriefs, then paste the summary into the runbook draft.
Keep Claude for drafting. Move any API automations off Sonnet 4.5 before its Nov 30 retirement.
Hold off on Gemini 4 Hydrogen until Google publishes a model card; keep Gemini 3.5 for now.
Add an optional 'AI red-team readiness' line item; OpenAI's Daybreak products will prompt client questions.
Test Office in Copilot when it reaches your tenant this month; compare against Gamma 5 on one real deck.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Add meeting-AI consent (Claude Meetings, Copilot, Gemini) and regional-use restrictions to the AI risk register template.

community.signal: Invisible text watermarking extended to more Claude models with no opt-out for paid users (~6.3K score, ~890 comments; week to Nov 3).
community.so_what: Client-facing text drafted in Claude may be detectable as AI-written. Disclose AI assistance in deliverables where contracts require it.

community.signal: Qwen's statement that its models will stay open source topped the week (~4.5K score), alongside a 2.8K-comment fight over Altman calling local inference a waste.
community.so_what: Open-weight options stay viable for clients who need fully on-prem AI in a DR scenario.

community.signal: Reports that Amazon is cancelling some GPU orders (~780 score).
community.so_what: Supply signals are mixed; don't build a client's AI recovery plan around a single cloud's GPU capacity.

community.signal: Threads on a false-positive ban wave and over-strict GPT-6 guardrails (Nov 7–8).
community.so_what: Account suspension is a real availability risk. Keep a second provider ready for critical workflows.

watch.title: Microsoft Ignite, Nov 17–20
watch.body: Expect Copilot routing (Chat / Cowork / Code), Teams @Copilot and agent governance news.

watch.title: Anthropic IPO prices week of Nov 16
watch.body: $70–78 range, ticker ANT, trading expected around Nov 19. Watch for any pricing or plan changes after listing.

watch.title: Nov 30: Sonnet 4.5 API retirement and Opus 4.8 fast-mode removal
watch.body: Move any scripts or client automations pinned to these models to Sonnet 5.5 or current Opus.

watch.title: Cursor without OpenAI models
watch.body: Confirm whether the Nov 12 cutoff took effect, and whether existing GPT models stay frozen or are removed.

watch.title: Nonprofit lawsuit to halt frontier AI
watch.body: Filed against OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceXAI. Low near-term impact, but worth one line in client AI vendor-risk notes.

sources: Sources consulted: OpenAI and Claude platform release notes, docs.x.ai, Microsoft 365 message center coverage, AI Weekly and a Nov 13 AI morning digest, Renaissance Capital, AI Signal Reddit digest (Nov 3), and coverage on the OpenAI–Cursor cutoff.
